posts.name: Snowball Captial ❄️☃️
posts.text:
I think Michael Burry is wrong to sell $FNMA and $FMCC common.

And I think Bill Ackman has the better map of how this ends.

Burry's Oct 11 note is clear: he sold the common, bought junior preferred, and flagged a Treasury conversion of the senior preferred (SPS) into common — dilution of 90%+.

That risk is real on paper.
I just don't think it's the base case the Trump team is trying to deliver.

Here's why I side with Ackman:

1. The SPS has already been paid — economically.

Fannie and Freddie drew about $193B from Treasury after 2008.
They have since returned about $301B in dividends.

Ackman's point is simple: treat the senior preferred as repaid, don't invent a brand-new dilution event to wipe out private common holders.

2. Ackman's path preserves the common.

His three-step plan:
→ Treasury / FHFA amend the PSPA so the SPS is treated as satisfied
→ Treasury exercises its warrants for ~79.9% of the common
→ Relist on the NYSE while conservatorship continues

Government control stays.
Mortgage markets aren't disrupted.
Existing common isn't vaporized by a 90% conversion.

That is "walk before you run," not "convert and crush."

3. Burry is hedging a scenario Ackman is fighting.

Burry's move makes sense if you believe Wall Street's conversion base case wins.
Preferred ranks above common if that happens.

But if the political goal is to show taxpayers a win, rebuild tradable equity, and keep housing finance quiet — converting SPS into a 90% wipeout of private common is a terrible headline.

It's the path that creates lawsuits, not a clean listing story.

4. Price action isn't the thesis.

Both stocks have given back most of the post-election rally.
Burry reads a head-and-shoulders.
I read a messy policy delay in a narrow AI-dominated market.

Weak charts don't settle who owns the economics of the GSEs.

My takeaway

Burry is brilliant at smelling risk.
Here, I think he's underweighting incentives.

A conversion that destroys private common may look neat in a spreadsheet.
It looks ugly in an administration that wants to claim it fixed Fannie and Freddie.

Ackman's framework asks a better question:
How do you end conservatorship without blowing up the mortgage market — and without stealing the residual that private capital already paid for once?

On that question, I think Ackman is closer to right.

$FNMA $FMCC

Sources:
Burry, Cassandra Unchained (Oct 11, 2026)
Ackman / Pershing Square commentary on the three-step GSE plan and SPS repayment

With the introduction of our Preferred Shares alongside our existing Ordinary Shares, we now have two distinct equities offering investors different ways to participate in the potential future success of Smarter Web. Model Benchmarks Are Worthless 

How can a model score 24% and 59% on the same 113 coding tasks?

It happens when you vary the harness that wraps it. 

I’ve increasingly ignored most of the recent model leaderboard results. Partly from exhaustion and partly because improvements in a ranking don’t show up in the actual work. 

So I asked the 8090 Labs team to measure what the leaderboards skip: the model and the harness together, on real bug fixes and features from open-source projects.

8090 Labs ran 7 models through 5 harnesses. 

Here are a few results I didn't expect:

- Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.1 scored 41% in Claude Code and 61% in OpenAI's Codex. It made 28 tool calls at the median in one and 66 in the other.

- The cheapest runs weren't the cheapest work. GLM in Codex cost $0.22 a run and $0.93 per success. In Pi it cost $0.25 a run and $0.43 per success.

- GLM passed a task on both attempts 51 times in one harness and 16 times in another.

- GPT-5.6 Sol and Grok 4.6 barely cared which harness they were in.

The bottom line is that if you're picking a model/harness combo off a model-only leaderboard, you're making a critical decision based on only half the information.

I don’t believe the volume of diesel Russia will export will affect the price. Moreover, we see that they can export from 300,000 to 500,000 tons a month today. Meanwhile, global consumption stands at 120 million tons a month. What kind of impact can that have? I don’t think it would have any. If some people think otherwise, so be it.

So I believe there are entirely different reasons behind these actions. If this is the approach, then why isn’t America making a “diesel deal” with Ukraine? Let Ukraine propose a “diesel deal.” We do have influence over whether these ships can sail or not, whether these refineries can operate or not. If that’s the case, then let’s do it.

Electricity is what matters to us. That’s clear. If we can be guaranteed protection for our power system, then we will not strike Russia’s diesel infrastructure in response. Electricity is first and foremost about helping people – keeping their lights on. It also means helping Europe. Everyone knows that we are connected to the European power grid. And if our energy infrastructure is not being destroyed, we can help some countries that are facing shortages by supplying them with cheaper electricity.

So, yes, let’s sign a corresponding “diesel deal” with the President of the United States.

From remarks at the Warsaw Security Forum. (1)

posts.text:
给大家推荐下这期播客！主持人是我现在的老板 @jposhaughnessy 嘉宾是我的线上导师 @sivers  Derek 过去一年多拒绝了所有播客邀请，这次只为 Jim 破例。简单总结下：

1️⃣Derek说孩子小的时候，父母像经理，要帮他做决定。但到了某个阶段，孩子会把你这个经理开除，你只能希望他以后愿意再请你回来当顾问。Jim 很认同，因为他 24 岁就当了爸爸，和太太定下的育儿目标只有一个：把孩子养成优秀的大人。所以他们不说“住我家就要听我的”。孩子问他问题，他常常指着书架说“自己去查”。多年后，他的三个孩子都说，这让他们养成了强烈的好奇心。

2️⃣Derek 每周给儿子 30 小时完全不分心的陪伴。儿子说：“我好像是唯一一个有爸爸的孩子。”Derek 说，这份陪伴也给了他视角：当所有人都在为选举、AI、新闻焦虑时，他知道什么才最重要。
现在儿子想去国外读寄宿学校，看中了日本的一所加拿大学校、印度泰米尔纳德邦的学校和泰国普吉岛的 UWC，申请全是他自己在做。

4️⃣ 让世界每个角落都像家
Derek 读到 Steve Pavlina 书里的一个观点：想持续成长，就要让自己感到意外，最极端的方式是搬到一个文化完全不同的地方。
快 40 岁卖掉公司后，他决定：前 40 年在美国生活，后 40 年在海外度过。每到一个地方，住到它真正像家，再离开。他的梦想是有一天转动地球仪，每个角落都像家。
在伦敦住了几个月后，他突然想买房子了，结果报价被拒反而让他顿时清醒过来：“有这种settle down 的感觉，就是该继续出发的时候。”
后来因为儿子，他在惠灵顿停留了 14 年。

5️⃣ 下一站：班加罗尔和上海
他说班加罗尔这座城市规划很糟，但那里的人是他见过最会聊天的。
他也很想住在中国，说中国城市的生活品质很高，从香港走过桥到深圳就像两个世界。他听一位在上海生活的塞尔维亚女士说，可以花几百美元在上海注册公司，请代理处理年检和税务，一年大约一千美元，再用自己的公司申请工作签证。他现在已经有了中文名：沈思问 和自己的咨询公司，打算以后在上海和班加罗尔两边住。
他推荐李稻葵的《中国的世界观》，说每个国家都是一种“被实践出来的哲学”。

6️⃣ 一生活出很多种人生
有人像欧姬芙，一辈子深挖一种风格；有人像毕加索，不停换阶段。Derek 属于后者。他希望临终回望时能说：看我住过多少地方，活过多少种人生。
他的书《How to Live》写了 27 种互相矛盾的活法，他说那本书就是他灵魂的样子。所以他对任何人生哲学都不评判，甚至想轮流试试贪婪、利他、享乐和谨慎的人生。

7️⃣ 心里的“确定性滑杆”
Derek 说，每个人对确定和未知的需求像一个滑杆，天性决定起点，处境会让它移动。他旅途中得了新冠，那几天只想回家，不想见任何新的人。从那以后，他更能理解那些“只想去熟悉的餐厅、看喜欢的剧、睡自己床”的人。
Jim 说，只有疯子才完全确定，连明天太阳升起也只是很高的概率。

8️⃣ 敢说“我不知道”
Jim 问：AI 能一键做出网站和产品后，执行力的稀缺价值在哪里？Derek 直接说：我不知道，没想过，不想随便乱讲。
Jim 说，曾有人因为他在电视上说了好几次“我不知道”而信任他。Derek 的邮件列表也是这样，没话说就十个月不发。

9️⃣ 探险家不适合当领队
Derek 承认自己以前是个糟糕的老板。他读完《Maverick》，第二天就宣布员工分红，两个月后又反悔，被员工骂惨。
他说跟着探险家很累，今天钻这个洞，明天退出来。现在他的建议是：探索留给自己，找到方向后，再给团队一条清楚的直线。

🔟 AI 可以让人更依赖，也可以更独立
Jim 常让 AI 替他反对的观点做最强辩护，几乎每次都发现对方有道理。他说人类发现火后没有禁止火，而是发明了火警和消防队。

quoted.text:
No, imo, it does not make sense to argue that Krugman's fiscal advice was right for France and the Eurozone in the 2010s. Those large deficits in the 2010s set the stage for today's looming fiscal crisis.  The high debt/gdp ratio today is the footprint of all those large deficits, in spite of the French government's low funding costs at the zero lower bound in the 2010s. 

Those large deficits certainly did not spur enough growth for France to simply grow out of the high debt/gdp ratio, contrary to what was advertised. 

Economists who were attacking "Eurozone austerity" in the 2010s should have realized that once the ECB stopped buying government bonds on a massive scale, the debt would be marked-to-market and bond yields might spike. That's exactly what's happening. All of the extra fiscal capacity is gone. And there is little spending room left for the core functions of the state (defense, education), which is crowded out by the growing interest expense and transfer payments (including pensions).

In any case, the fiscal lesson is that yields in bond markets jump, but the debt/gdp ratio is a slow-moving variable.
